title: add profiling baselines and representative workload runners v19
author: Anya Patel
description: Context: Benchmark lab needs updated profiling baselines and a set of representative workload runners that cover long-form generation, chat-style multi-turn, and embedding-heavy inference for the LLaMA and Mistral families. Motivation: recent runtime kernel changes (ENG-1267) changed latency/throughput characteristics; we need new baselines and representative runners to detect regressions in nightly profiling and to feed the reporting pipeline. Summary of changes: 1) Add new profiling baselines for sequence lengths 512/2048/4096 with quantization-aware flags and hotpath annotations. 2) Add representative workload runners for llama-2-7b, llama-2-13b, and mistral-7b including prompt templates, input distributions, and validation tasks. 3) Wire baselines into the existing reporting pipeline (benchmark-lab/reports) with new dashboard metrics and CSV export. 4) Add CI job (benchmark-lab/profiling) to run quick smoke profiles on PRs against a small sample. Checklist: - [x] Add baseline configs and runner harness - [x] Integrate results uploader to reporting pipeline - [x] Add unit tests for runner input validation - [x] Add CI smoke job and gating config - [x] Update docs/benchmark-lab/README.md Migration notes: Baselines are additive and stored under benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v19; no breaking changes to existing consumers. Related: ENG-1267, PM-342. Docs: docs/benchmark-lab/README.md updated with runner examples. CI notes: first run failed due to missing runner dependency, reran with pinned docker image and all checks passed. Merge method: squash and merge.
commits: 3 commits: (1) add v19 profiling baseline configs and sample traces, (2) add representative workload runners and templates, (3) integrate reporting pipeline uploader and dashboard mapping
